minutes.headline: Stormwater Task Force will invite its engineering consultants to the next meeting to map out a stormwater utility.
minutes.summary: A resident described repeated stormwater flooding on Page Street during public comment, and members discussed causes and the lack of an easy fix. The task force then reviewed Chelmsford's stormwater utility materials, how to set up an enterprise fund, fees, staffing and outreach, and agreed to hear from the consultants before going to the town manager. The only vote was adjournment.

public_comment.topic: Stormwater flooding down her driveway and Page Street into Beaver Brook; unmaintained Village of Flat Hill retention pond, new development runoff, private sump pumps draining into town drains, and a request that residents be kept in mind in planning.

budget_items.what_was_said: Members estimated a new drainage system would cost a very large sum, from hundreds of thousands to millions.

budget_items.topic: ARPA funds for Flat Hill retention pond
budget_items.what_was_said: Select board discussed using ARPA money, but the pond is on private HOA property and the trustees declined.
Piping water through neighboring property was described as a very large price tag.
Chelmsford used flat funding; a Massachusetts asset management grant and community compact grant were raised as possible sources.
Chelmsford's budget included new employees, equipment and capital outlay, with fees on sewer bills; annual budget estimated at a couple million.
Fines to other towns for permit noncompliance were noted.
Chelmsford uses tiered fees based on impervious surface; households and businesses split the cost.
One stormwater project was above the cutoff on the proposed capital plan, with others also on it; an engineer is being lined up for design.
Chelmsford discounts the rate for property owners with maintained stormwater BMPs.

what_happened.line: The task force agreed to hear from the town's engineering consultants before approaching the town manager about a stormwater utility.
The DPW director will ask the consultants to attend the next meeting, expected on the third Thursday, the 15th.
Members set a goal of having a stormwater utility proposal ready for town meeting, and the DPW director will prepare a preliminary budget, staffing and project list.
Members reviewed Chelmsford's utility, which charges tiered fees on sewer bills by impervious surface, and discussed how to set up an enterprise fund.
A resident described repeated flooding on Page Street during public comment; members discussed causes and said no easy fix exists. The only vote was adjournment.

why_it_matters: A stormwater utility would likely mean a new fee on property owners, possibly shown on the sewer bill, so residents may be asked to vote on it at town meeting.
The Page Street flooding and the cost of a drainage fix, which members called very large, are the problem a utility would be built to pay for.
